clues.title: Letter from Whittle & Cross
clues.description: A letter from the firm Whittle & Cross, delivered this morning and found already opened on Isabella's desk: 'Confirming our appointment at 09:30 today to review irregularities in the bookshop partnership transfer documents.' Isabella had found something wrong — and had booked a solicitor.

clues.title: Forged partnership transfer document
clues.description: In the safe behind the loose back panel: a signed transfer document putting the bookshop expansion in Priya's name. The signature reads 'I. Reed' but the loop on the capital R is reversed — inconsistent with every other sample of Isabella's handwriting in the room.

clues.title: Green thread on the rear door latch
clues.description: A single thread of emerald-green wool caught on the sharp edge of the bookshop's rear door latch. The same shade as Priya's scarf — and the scarf, still hanging on the stockroom hook, has a small pulled loop on one end.

clues.title: Glass broke from inside
clues.description: The broken window pane in the back room: large shards and the frame splinter lie inside the room. Only smaller fragments are outside in the alley. A genuine break-in would show the opposite. Someone broke this pane from inside to simulate forced entry.

clues.title: Letter opener — wiped clean and replaced
clues.description: The Victorian letter opener in the pen pot on Isabella's desk. Despite being the nearest heavy implement to the wound, it shows no fingerprints at all — it has been recently wiped. And the pen pot stands slightly off its usual ring-mark, as if hurriedly returned.

clues.title: Invoice timestamp mismatch
clues.description: The delivery invoice on the stockroom table is signed by Priya at 08:10. The driver's carbon copy, however, records the delivery complete at 08:05. Five minutes are unaccounted for — and those five minutes are inside the murder window.

clues.title: Solicitor's letter delivered sealed
clues.description: Ruth confirms she pushed the Whittle & Cross letter through the bookshop door sealed and unopened at 07:10. By 08:00, Priya had already read it — before Isabella arrived. Priya knew exactly what Isabella was about to bring to the solicitor.

clues.title: A crash from the bookshop back room
clues.description: Ruth heard a sharp crash — like furniture going over — from the back of the bookshop at around 08:40 while she was finishing her round along the rear alley. She assumed it was boxes falling in the stockroom.

clues.title: Isabella arrived early and went straight inside
clues.description: Elias saw Isabella arrive at 08:32, nearly half an hour before her usual opening time. She didn't stop to talk to anyone — just went directly in. Something had brought her in early.

clues.title: Owen lingered at the bookshop window
clues.description: Elias noticed Owen pausing at the bookshop window at 08:25, a rolled-up letter in hand. Owen had received a new debt-demand notice from Isabella that morning.

clues.title: Owen's debt folder in Isabella's desk
clues.description: A folder in Isabella's drawer: letters to Owen Price demanding repayment of a personal loan by month's end, with a note in Isabella's hand — 'next step: solicitor, 11th.' Today is the 11th.

clues.title: Owen was in his yard all morning
clues.description: Owen was pouring a concrete pad in his yard from 07:00 until 09:30 — the concrete needed constant tending and two of his lads were with him the whole time. He never went near the bookshop.

clues.title: Ben noticed the broken window
clues.description: Ben mentioned to someone at the cafe at 09:00 that the bookshop's back window looked broken. He'd seen it when he passed the alley at about 08:50 on his way back to the van — after the murder.

clues.title: Priya claims she was shelving stock all morning
clues.description: Priya says she was in the stockroom from 07:00 until Nadia arrived. But she cannot account for the gap between 08:10 (when the invoice was signed) and 08:48 (when she was heard shelving books).

clues.title: Loose thread on Priya's scarf
clues.description: Priya's green scarf hangs in the stockroom. Inspect it closely: one end has a small pulled loop, matching exactly the thread snagged on the rear door latch — same weight, same shade, same twist direction.

conclusions.summary: Priya had forged Isabella's signature on the partnership transfer. Isabella had discovered this and booked a solicitor. Priya read the letter before Isabella arrived — she knew she had hours.
Priya was in the bookshop alone with Isabella during the murder window. Her invoice alibi has a 40-minute gap. The green thread puts her at the rear door she claims not to have used.
The letter opener was the nearest heavy object and has been recently wiped clean — it was used and returned.
Isabella was struck with the Victorian letter opener in the back room at approximately 08:43.
The broken window was staged from the inside to suggest an unknown intruder. The glass distribution proves it.
Priya's claim to have been in the stockroom all morning is undermined by the invoice gap and the thread on the rear door.
Owen had a significant debt to Isabella that was due today and was seen lingering outside the bookshop in anger.
Owen was in his yard pouring concrete with two workers present from 07:00 until 09:30.
